fitnessSpec.hiking: strong, sustained multi-day alpine fitness; long approach via Ptarmigan Ridge to Camp Kiser plus additional glaciated approach to the Pleiades ridge before any technical climbing begins
fitnessSpec.packWeight: overnight/glacier kit expected - rope, crevasse rescue hardware, camping gear; roughly 35-45+ lb pack on the approach

partner_requirements.approachTime: long, multi-day approach - miles of trail and glacier travel to Camp Kiser via Ptarmigan Ridge, then further glacier/snow travel toward the Pleiades ridge; not a day-trip from the trailhead for most parties
requiredSkills: judgment for rapid weather changes high on the Baker massif
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: advanced/experienced alpine climber - comfortable with unroped Class 3 scrambling on loose rock and with roped glacier travel; not appropriate for a first alpine objective

weather.typical: Cascade volcanic-massif weather: conditions can change rapidly high on Baker's shoulder terrain
weather.probability: Afternoon cloud buildup and fast-moving weather deterioration are common on the Baker massif in summer; the exposed Ptarmigan Ridge approach adds wind exposure

seasonal_hazards.exposure: Moderate-high: friable volcanic rock on the Class 3 summit scramble combines with glacier travel exposure below it - a slip on loose rock or an unroped misstep near crevasses could have serious consequences, compounded by the risk of rapid weather changes

avalanche.zone: NWAC West Slopes North (regional zone covering the Mount Baker massif; no forecast zone specifically names the Pleiades)

seasonal_hazards.crevasses: Active glacier travel is required near the peak; roped travel and crevasse rescue skills are necessary, with snow bridges generally more solid early in the July-August window and weaker by late summer

July.reason: Within the best-season window; more consolidated glacier travel and typically the most stable Cascade summer weather

June.reason: Snowpack often still deep on the approach and access road may have residual snow; glacier crossings can be more complex and weather less settled than mid-summer

August.reason: Within the best-season window; driest rock conditions for the Class 3 summit scramble, though crevasses become more open late in the month

September.reason: Outside the best-season window; crevasses more open and snow bridges less reliable, shorter daylight, and higher chance of early-season snow at elevation

crowds.peakTraffic: rarely climbed; if any traffic occurs it would cluster in the July-August optimal window, likely as a side objective for parties already in Ptarmigan Ridge/Camp Kiser terrain
crowds.estimatePerSeason: unknown - low-traffic; likely well under 10 parties/season based on remoteness (no trip reports found; the Pleiades is overshadowed by standard Mt. Baker routes and even by nearby named objectives like the Cockscomb and Border Peaks that share the Ptarmigan Ridge approach)

pitch_detail.notes: 3.6 miles roundtrip from Twin Lakes, 765 ft gain. Well-marked trail with switchbacks and cliff traverses. Wildflowers in summer. Water available at lakes and streams en route.
pitch_detail.pitch: Approach: Twin Lakes to High Pass

pitch_detail.notes: Off-trail scree/snow slope climb NNE, gaining ~400-500 ft to col. In early season, may be steep snow requiring care for avalanche (crevasse unlikely but snow is wet and heavy). By August, usually dry scree.
pitch_detail.pitch: High Pass to South Col (Larrabee Col)

pitch_detail.notes: Traverse basin ~0.5 mile, descend slightly, then climb gully system to notch. Gully is loose and narrow in places, Class 2-3 scrambling. ~30-45 minutes from col.

From notch, traverse ~50 ft east and ascend Class 2-3 scramble to summit. Excellent panoramic views. Return to notch and descend via descent gully (black lichen-covered rocky gully to the east, no rappel needed).

From notch, ascend to goat ledge and traverse the ledge to link peaks 3 and 4. Peak 1 (west) requires Class 3+ scramble with exposure, slabby sections, and knife-edge ridge. Peak 3 accessible via ledge; peak 4 at far end of ledge traverse. Extreme care on ledge due to loose rock.

before.detailed_rack: No technical rock climbing gear required; this is a scramble. Bring a helmet and grippy footwear (rock shoes or sticky approach shoes). Trekking poles helpful for scree. Microspikes or crampons if snow present. No rope, protection, or belay gear needed.
pro_tips: Tag Peak 2 (the easy, westernmost peak) if you just want one summit with the least risk — it's the one 'average' scramblers can realistically expect to reach.
For Peak 3, the true highest and most prominent summit, look for a climbable gully roughly halfway along the exposed goat ledge — the actual high point is easy to walk past.
Call the Glacier Public Service Center, (360) 599-2714, before you drive — the last 2 miles of FS-3065 wash out frequently and may force you to start from the Yellow Aster Butte trailhead instead.
Go in a stable weather window and keep parties tight in gullies — this rock is consistently rated among the worst in the Cascades.

approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From Glacier, WA, drive east about 12 miles on SR 542 (Mt. Baker Highway) to the WSDOT Shuksan maintenance facility and turn onto Twin Lakes Road (FS-3065).

itinerary.cal: Twin Lakes road is often snow-covered or rough into early summer; conditions are typically best August-September once the talus and rock are dry.

days.note: From the Twin Lakes trailhead, climbers contour past Gold Run/Low Pass beneath Mount Larrabee's east ridge to reach the base of the Pleiades, then scramble exposed, notoriously loose 3rd/4th class rock to the summit. Nearly everyone treats this as a long single day rather than an overnight — Twin Lakes already sits near 5,200 ft, and there's no established camp or reliable water any closer to the peaks.
days.title: Car-to-car scramble to The Pleiades

schedule.label: Leave Twin Lakes trailhead
schedule.detail: High-clearance/4WD is often needed on the final rough miles of the Twin Lakes road, especially early season.

schedule.label: Reach Gold Run / Low Pass area
schedule.detail: Traverse meadows and talus below Mount Larrabee's east ridge toward the Pleiades saddle.

schedule.label: Gain the base of the Pleiades ridge
schedule.detail: Helmets on here; the rock quality gets notably worse from this point.

schedule.label: Scramble to the summit
schedule.detail: Exposed 3rd/4th class climbing on chossy blocks and a short slab pitch to the 'goat ledge'; parties note this stretch commonly takes 2-3x longer than expected.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Highpoint of the group at 7,371 ft.

schedule.label: Down-climb and return to trailhead
schedule.detail: No rappel route is established — reverse the ascent line carefully; loose rock makes the descent rockfall-prone for parties below.

days.objective: Reach the high point of The Pleiades via the Twin Lakes / Gold Run Pass approach

itinerary.totalNote: A long, technical single day: roughly 7.5 miles round trip with about 3,200 ft of gain/loss, but slow going (9-11 hrs car to car) due to sustained loose 3rd/4th class scrambling near the summit.
